script:
This is the New Saint Croix Union for Monday, October 5. Here is the week's news.

Oakdale's planning commission met Thursday night on fifty-five rental townhomes at a former Par 3 the city's plan still guides as open space.

Mulcahy Holdings wants the units at fifty-five eighty-five Golfview Avenue North, the old Oakdale Par 3. The ask is a comprehensive plan amendment, a planned unit development amendment, a preliminary plat, and a site plan. Staff recommended approval of each. The commission holds the hearing and recommends to the city council. Council action is expected October 27.

The comprehensive plan guides the property as open space. Allowed uses in that category are undeveloped publicly owned land and wetlands. The request would re-guide it to medium density residential, four to thirty units an acre. Proposed density is about ten units an acre, with protected wetland left out of the count. Zoning is The Greens of Silver Lake planned unit development, which designates the site for open space and recreational use. The amendment would apply R-3 townhome standards.

The parcel is about forty-four point six acres. Buildable area is about five point one acres. The remainder is about thirty-nine point five acres. A structure and a remnant parking lot are still there. Access is from Fifty-sixth Street North. The townhomes would be tied to Cedric's Landing apartments and share some amenities. The units are proposed as market rate, not income restricted.

Private streets would dead-end about eight hundred feet from Fifty-sixth Street North and Golfview Avenue North. The code maximum for a dead-end street is three hundred feet. Proposed width is twenty-four feet from back of curb to back of curb. The city standard is twenty-four feet of pavement, usually measured face of curb to face of curb, so the section is two feet narrower. The developer is asking the council to allow the longer dead end and the narrower street.

Projected traffic is four hundred fifty to five hundred fifty trips a day. A traffic study is still required at Fifty-sixth and Highway 120, also called Century Avenue. A September environmental assessment found possible contamination from herbicides, fungicides, pesticides, and fertilizers on former greens and tees. Mercury was detected at three former greens. Lead was detected at the maintenance building. Conditions include cleanup to residential standards. Mulcahy Holdings has not requested city financial assistance. The hearing was at seven at the Oakdale Discovery Center.

Lake Elmo's council holds a public hearing Tuesday on a grading permit at ten thousand eight hundred thirty Stillwater Boulevard North.

Frattalone Companies wants to move about sixty thousand cubic yards of earth on the site, two thousand, seven hundred twenty-seven cubic yards per acre. The request includes importing fill, earthwork, and stormwater work on the property. The hearing is at seven at City Hall, thirty-eight eighty Laverne Avenue North. Handwritten comments may be mailed by five the Wednesday before the meeting. Email comments go to Sophia Jensen by noon on the day of the meeting.

The same evening, Lake Elmo's council meets at six in closed session on offers for city-owned property, parcel 160292124000. The session is to develop or consider offers or counteroffers for the sale. Members may participate remotely. The meeting is at thirty-eight eighty Laverne Avenue North.

Washington County's board meets Tuesday on an eighty-eight thousand, ninety-two dollar state grant to put a solar array on Park Grove Library. The project, installation included, is one hundred forty-six thousand, eight hundred twenty dollars. The grant would leave the county fifty-eight thousand, seven hundred twenty-eight dollars.

Public Works recommends the grant agreement. If the board approves it, the public works director would approve a pending contract with Apadana Solar Technologies, contingent on the grant. Estimated utility savings are six thousand, two hundred forty-one dollars a year. The printed return is nine point four years. The printed system life is thirty years. The county already received fifty-three thousand, nine hundred sixty-five dollars under the Solar on Public Buildings program.

The same consent calendar would extend an inmate-housing agreement with the Hennepin County Sheriff's Office through December 31, 2027. It now ends October 11, 2026. Hennepin County would pay seventy-five dollars a day for each inmate in custody. Washington County does not have to lease a bed if the jail has no space. The board meets at nine in the morning in the County Board Room.

Stillwater's council meets Tuesday night on assessments for the 2026 Street Improvement Project, the 2026 Sidewalk Rehabilitation Project, and County State Aid Highway 5 Phase 4. A second hearing covers delinquent cleanup fees, citations, lodging tax, parking fees, plan review fees, solid waste fees, and utility bills. A Series 2026B bond resolution is marked available Tuesday.

Consent includes a conditional use permit for a private gym in the central business district at two-twenty Commercial Street, and an interim use permit for a food truck at two-twenty-five Main Street North. A short-term rental license is listed for two-twenty-five Martha Street North. The workshop includes a facility study and concept plans for Lily Lake Ice Arena. A closed session is listed on the assessment appeal Allan LaValier versus the City of Stillwater. A proposed land exchange between the Department of Natural Resources and the National Park Service is on the consent list. The workshop is at four-thirty. The regular meeting is at seven.

School District 622 holds a work study tonight at six on the MCA achievement report and elementary math. Study sessions are open to the public and do not allow public comment. Luckner presents the MCA Achievement Report and calendar changes. The superintendent check-in covers enrollment, an elementary math update, and superintendent goals. The session is at the 622 Education Center, twenty-five twenty East Twelfth Avenue, North St. Paul.

The Town of Hudson board meets Wednesday at six on a proposed ordinance regulating data centers, and on a fifty-acre parcel gifted to the Boosters. American Polywater is up for a special exception for a manufacturing facility at parcel 020-1076-20-000. Cedar Medows is up for a preliminary plat. Cedar Meadows is up for a rezone of two parcels in that certified survey map from residential to agricultural residential. Affolter is up for a four-lot certified survey map on Brummel Road. Bueno Street Kitchen is applying for a Class B beer and Class C wine combination license. The meeting is at the Hudson Town Hall, nine eighty County Road A. A budget workshop follows.

Woodbury's council meets Wednesday on an interim solar permit and on rules for keeping chickens. The planning commission reviewed the USS Mazur Solar application September 28 and recommended approval, seven to zero. Staff concur and recommend the permit. US Solar wants a community solar garden at eleven thousand eight hundred sixty Dale Road Court, panels on about twenty-seven acres, north of Dale Road and west of Manning Avenue. The property is zoned R-1, urban reserve. A hearing the same night covers amendments on chicken coops. Bills of one million, four hundred seventy-six thousand, eight hundred forty-one dollars and forty-four cents from September 11, and four million, four hundred eighteen thousand, five hundred sixty-two dollars and five cents from September 18, are up for approval. The meeting is at seven-thirty, virtual and in the Council Chambers at Woodbury City Hall. Open forum speakers get three minutes, inside a twenty-minute cap.

Woodbury's parks commission meets Tuesday on a playground replacement at Powers Lake East Park. An online questionnaire drew seventeen responses. Most respondents reported children ages three to eleven and a visit at least once a week. Staff developed three concepts and wants the commission to say which two should go to a final community review. The playground is classified as small. The existing concrete footprint is the play area. An optional tour starts at six at La Lake Park South, sixty-seven forty-eight Military Road. The meeting is at seven at the M Health Fairview Sports Center, upper-level conference room, forty-one twenty-five Radio Drive. It is in person only.

The forty-ninth Rivertown Fall Art Festival filled Lowell Park in downtown Stillwater on Saturday and Sunday. Hours were ten to five both days. The Greater Stillwater Chamber of Commerce puts it on along the St. Croix at two-oh-one Water Street. It is a juried fine-art fair. The chamber says more than two hundred artists and makers showed handcrafted work. Besides the booths, the chamber lists a beer-and-wine tent, local food vendors, and live music. As of the chamber's 2026 pages, the music schedule and the named food-vendor list were not posted. The chamber puts expected attendance above ten thousand.

Times and documents are in the show notes.
